en: I see. So you pulled the lever, Joker?{PAGE}The cart will miss the five workers,{SAUT}and instead kill the single worker{SAUT}on the other track...
Sacrificing one to save five, huh...?{PAGE}Well, it saves the most lives.{SAUT}I guess that's a kind of "correct."
H-Hang on a sec!{PAGE}So that innocent guy just gets run{SAUT}over? Man, I don't know if saving{SAUT}those guys makes it okay...
I agree. You can't measure the value{SAUT}of human life in numbers alone.{PAGE}I suppose that's what makes this{SAUT}problem so difficult.
Yes. Queen summed it up best―{SAUT}There's no objectively right answer.{PAGE}All we can do is keep in mind{SAUT}everything we've considered,{SAUT}then move forward.
I see. So you chose not to pull{SAUT}the lever, Joker?{PAGE}The cart will continue on its path,{SAUT}and hit those five people... But the{SAUT}one other person will be spared.
I-Is that really okay? I mean,{SAUT}wouldn't it be better to save five{SAUT}people instead of just one...?{PAGE}Arrgh, I don't get it! We can't just{SAUT}kill that other guy, either!
If we do not make a sacrifice, then{SAUT}we cannot save another...{PAGE}A condition of remarkable cruelty.
I don't know what I'd do if I were{SAUT}actually in that situation...
Well, like I said, there isn't an{SAUT}answer that's objectively "right"{SAUT}here.{PAGE}All we can do is keep in mind{SAUT}everything we've considered,{SAUT}then move forward.
